quick.summary: How to reload a year of history without breaking today’s run.
quick.takeaway: One day at a time. Replace, check, move on.

beats.line: I need to reload a whole year after a bug fix. One big run tonight?
If it fails at month eleven, you start again. Slice it.
First, run one day at a time, oldest first.
Second, each run replaces that day. It never adds on top.
Third, check each day’s row count before the next.
Fourth, keep it away from today’s scheduled run.
Three hundred small runs sounds slower than one.
Slower to start, faster to finish. A failure costs one day, not the year.
Day by day, replacing each one, with a count check between.
And tomorrow’s report still arrives on time.

quiz.question: Why reload history one day at a time?
options: A failure costs one day, not the whole reload
It makes the data more accurate
quiz.explanation: Small slices can be checked and rerun on their own, so one failure does not undo everything.

quiz.question: During a reload, each run should add its rows on top of what is already there.
quiz.explanation: Adding on top double counts. Each run should replace its own day.
